// fx.h
#pragma once
// Generated by logue-patcher's logue-codegen.
// NOT hand-written -- do not edit directly, re-export instead.
#include "processor.h"
#include "unit_delfx.h"
#include <cmath>

// Effects link no oscillator API -- stand-ins for the two symbols primitives use.
#define osc_sinf fx_sinf
static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) float osc_w0f_for_note(uint8_t note, uint8_t mod)
{
  const float f = 440.f * fastpow2f(((float)note + (float)mod * (1.f / 255.f) - 69.f) * (1.f / 12.f));
  return (f < 23679.643054f ? f : 23679.643054f) * (1.f / 48000.f);
}

class Fx : public Processor
{
public:
  // Floats of SDRAM unit_init allocates and hands to init().
  uint32_t getBufferSize() const override final { return 32768u; }

  void setParameter(uint8_t index, int32_t value) override final
  {
    switch (index)
    {
    case 0: time01_ = param_10bit_to_f32(value); break;
    case 1: depth01_ = param_10bit_to_f32(value); break;
    case 2: mix01_ = (value + 1000) * (1.f / 2000.f); break;
    default: break;
    }
  }

  void init(float *sdram) override final
  {
    sdram_n = sdram + 0;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 32768u; ++i) sdram[i] = 0.f;
    note_ = 60.f;
    noteFine_ = 0.f;
    tempo_ = 120.f;
    time01_ = 0.f;
    depth01_ = 0.f;
    mix01_ = 0.5f;
    for (int k = 0; k < 5; ++k) grainSt_n[k] = 0u;
    prevTrig_n = 0.f;
    hold_n = 0.f;
    last_n = 0.f;
    positionPercent_n = 0;
    sizePercent_n = 50;
    fadePercent_n = 10;
    grainLen_n = (2) >= 2 ? 65536u : (2) >= 1 ? 32768u : 16384u;
  }

  // Korg's README: clear delay lines and state, keep param values (len_ and the dials stay).
  void reset() override final
  {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 32768u; ++i) sdram_n[i] = 0.f;
    for (int k = 0; k < 5; ++k) grainSt_n[k] = 0u;
    prevTrig_n = 0.f;
    hold_n = 0.f;
    last_n = 0.f;
  }

  void setTempo(float bpm) override final { tempo_ = bpm; }

  // Every input sample is read before the frame's outputs are written: the SDK allows the
  // firmware to pass one buffer as both in and out.
  void process(const float *in, float *out, uint32_t frames) override final
  {
    (void)in;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < frames; ++i)
    {
      float y_n = 0.f;
      out[2 * i] = clip1m1f(y_n);
      out[2 * i + 1] = clip1m1f(y_n);
    }
  }

private:
  // The note a primitive that follows the played note (an oscillator's pitch, a TRACK filter)
  // reads: an effect gets none, so it's a fixed middle C.
  float note_;
  float noteFine_;
  // The fixed knobs' positions (0..1), as the device reports them.
  float time01_;
  float depth01_;
  float mix01_;
  // The device tempo in BPM, 120 until the device gives one.
  float tempo_;
  float *sdram_n;
  uint32_t grainSt_n[5];
  float prevTrig_n;
  float hold_n;
  float last_n;
  float positionPercent_n;
  float sizePercent_n;
  float fadePercent_n;
  uint32_t grainLen_n;

  // One sample of a looping grain (util/grain). st: [0] index, [1] length (0 = nothing yet),
  // [2] delay, [3] fade, [4] capturing. On a rising trig -- or, with selfTrig, at the start of
  // every pass -- it latches the delay (position 0..1 of the buffer, 1 = oldest), the length (size,
  // in samples) and the fade (0..1 of half the grain), then for length samples copies the buffer
  // at that constant delay into its own table (int16 over +-2, like the buffer), a fade-in and
  // fade-out of fade samples baked in, and afterwards loops the table until the next trigger.
  // What was playing at the trigger (*last) ramps out over the fade, so a retrigger doesn't
  // click. Inlined (always_inline): a call with its fourteen arguments cost more than much of
  // the body in grain-mill (xd emulator, 2026-10-01); code grows by a copy per voice.
  static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) float grain_step(const int16_t *buf, uint32_t mask, uint32_t w, int16_t *table, uint32_t tableLen, uint32_t *st, float *prevTrig, float *hold, float *last, float trig, int selfTrig, float positionPercent, float sizePercent, float fadePercent)
  {
    const float gate = trig >= 0.5f ? 1.f : 0.f;
    int start = gate > *prevTrig;
    *prevTrig = gate;
    if (selfTrig && !st[4] && st[0] == 0u) start = 1;
    if (start)
    {
      *hold = *last;
      // Position and size are only ever read here, so the clamps and SIZE's cube cost nothing
      // between triggers (they used to be computed every sample: +40 cycles a voice on the xd).
      const float p = positionPercent < 0.f ? 0.f : (positionPercent > 100.f ? 1.f : positionPercent * 0.01f);
      st[2] = 1u + (uint32_t)(p * (float)mask);
      const float t = sizePercent < 0.f ? 0.f : (sizePercent > 100.f ? 1.f : sizePercent * 0.01f);
      uint32_t len = 480u + (uint32_t)((float)(tableLen - 480u) * t * t * t);
      if (len > tableLen) len = tableLen;
      st[1] = len;
      const float f = fadePercent < 0.f ? 0.f : (fadePercent > 100.f ? 1.f : fadePercent * 0.01f);
      st[3] = 16u + (uint32_t)(f * (float)(len / 2u - 16u));
      st[4] = 1u;
      st[0] = 0u;
    }
    const uint32_t len = st[1];
    if (len == 0u) { *last = 0.f; return 0.f; }
    const uint32_t i = st[0];
    const uint32_t fl = st[3];
    const float toFloat = 1.f / 16383.f;
    if (st[4])
    {
      float att = 1.f;
      if (i < fl) att = (float)i / (float)fl;
      if (len - i <= fl) { const float a = (float)(len - i) / (float)fl; if (a < att) att = a; }
      float x = (float)buf[(w - st[2]) & mask] * toFloat * att;
      if (x > 2.f) x = 2.f; else if (x < -2.f) x = -2.f;
      table[i] = (int16_t)(x * 16383.f + (x < 0.f ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
    }
    float out = (float)table[i] * toFloat;
    if (st[4] && i < fl) out += *hold * (1.f - (float)i / (float)fl);
    *last = out;
    if (++st[0] >= len) { st[0] = 0u; st[4] = 0u; }
    return out;
  }
};

// Effects link no oscillator API -- stand-ins for the two symbols primitives use.

class Fx : public Processor
{
public:
  // Floats of SDRAM unit_init allocates and hands to init().
  uint32_t getBufferSize() const override final { return 98304u; }

  void setParameter(uint8_t index, int32_t value) override final
  {
    switch (index)
    {
    case 0: time01_ = param_10bit_to_f32(value); break;
    case 1: depth01_ = param_10bit_to_f32(value); break;
    case 2: mix01_ = (value + 1000) * (1.f / 2000.f); break;
    default: break;
    }
  }

  void init(float *sdram) override final
  {
    sdram_n = sdram + 0;
    sdram_c_buf = sdram + 32768;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 98304u; ++i) sdram[i] = 0.f;
    note_ = 60.f;
    noteFine_ = 0.f;
    tempo_ = 120.f;
    time01_ = 0.f;
    depth01_ = 0.f;
    mix01_ = 0.5f;
    for (int k = 0; k < 5; ++k) grainSt_n[k] = 0u;
    prevTrig_n = 0.f;
    hold_n = 0.f;
    last_n = 0.f;
    bufW_c_buf = 0u;
    freezeLevel_c_buf = 0.f;
    value_c_trig = 37 * 0.01f;
    value_c_position = 37 * 0.01f;
    value_c_size = 37 * 0.01f;
    positionPercent_n = 0;
    sizePercent_n = 50;
    fadePercent_n = 10;
    grainLen_n = (2) >= 2 ? 65536u : (2) >= 1 ? 32768u : 16384u;
    bufLen_c_buf = (2) >= 3 ? 262144u : (2) >= 2 ? 131072u : (2) >= 1 ? 65536u : 32768u;
    freeze_c_buf = 0;
  }

  // Korg's README: clear delay lines and state, keep param values (len_ and the dials stay).
  void reset() override final
  {
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 32768u; ++i) sdram_n[i] = 0.f;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < 65536u; ++i) sdram_c_buf[i] = 0.f;
    for (int k = 0; k < 5; ++k) grainSt_n[k] = 0u;
    prevTrig_n = 0.f;
    hold_n = 0.f;
    last_n = 0.f;
    bufW_c_buf = 0u;
    freezeLevel_c_buf = 0.f;
  }

  void setTempo(float bpm) override final { tempo_ = bpm; }

  // Every input sample is read before the frame's outputs are written: the SDK allows the
  // firmware to pass one buffer as both in and out.
  void process(const float *in, float *out, uint32_t frames) override final
  {
    (void)in;
      float y_c_trig = value_c_trig;
      float y_c_position = value_c_position;
      float y_c_size = value_c_size;
    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < frames; ++i)
    {
      float y_n = grain_step(((const int16_t *)sdram_c_buf), (bufLen_c_buf - 1u), bufW_c_buf, (int16_t *)sdram_n, grainLen_n, grainSt_n, &prevTrig_n, &hold_n, &last_n, y_c_trig, 0, (positionPercent_n + (y_c_position) * 50.f), (sizePercent_n + (y_c_size) * 50.f), fadePercent_n);
      out[2 * i] = clip1m1f(y_n);
      out[2 * i + 1] = clip1m1f(y_n);
      buffer_write((int16_t *)sdram_c_buf, bufLen_c_buf - 1u, &bufW_c_buf, 0.f, (freeze_c_buf >= 1.f ? 1.f : 0.f), &freezeLevel_c_buf);
    }
  }

private:
  // The note a primitive that follows the played note (an oscillator's pitch, a TRACK filter)
  // reads: an effect gets none, so it's a fixed middle C.
  float note_;
  float noteFine_;
  // The fixed knobs' positions (0..1), as the device reports them.
  float time01_;
  float depth01_;
  float mix01_;
  // The device tempo in BPM, 120 until the device gives one.
  float tempo_;
  float *sdram_n;
  float *sdram_c_buf;
  float value_c_trig;
  float value_c_position;
  float value_c_size;
  uint32_t grainSt_n[5];
  float prevTrig_n;
  float hold_n;
  float last_n;
  float positionPercent_n;
  float sizePercent_n;
  float fadePercent_n;
  uint32_t grainLen_n;
  uint32_t bufLen_c_buf;
  uint32_t bufW_c_buf;
  float freezeLevel_c_buf;
  float freeze_c_buf;

  // One sample of a looping grain (util/grain). st: [0] index, [1] length (0 = nothing yet),
  // [2] delay, [3] fade, [4] capturing. On a rising trig -- or, with selfTrig, at the start of
  // every pass -- it latches the delay (position 0..1 of the buffer, 1 = oldest), the length (size,
  // in samples) and the fade (0..1 of half the grain), then for length samples copies the buffer
  // at that constant delay into its own table (int16 over +-2, like the buffer), a fade-in and
  // fade-out of fade samples baked in, and afterwards loops the table until the next trigger.
  // What was playing at the trigger (*last) ramps out over the fade, so a retrigger doesn't
  // click. Inlined (always_inline): a call with its fourteen arguments cost more than much of
  // the body in grain-mill (xd emulator, 2026-10-01); code grows by a copy per voice.
  static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) float grain_step(const int16_t *buf, uint32_t mask, uint32_t w, int16_t *table, uint32_t tableLen, uint32_t *st, float *prevTrig, float *hold, float *last, float trig, int selfTrig, float positionPercent, float sizePercent, float fadePercent)
  {
    const float gate = trig >= 0.5f ? 1.f : 0.f;
    int start = gate > *prevTrig;
    *prevTrig = gate;
    if (selfTrig && !st[4] && st[0] == 0u) start = 1;
    if (start)
    {
      *hold = *last;
      // Position and size are only ever read here, so the clamps and SIZE's cube cost nothing
      // between triggers (they used to be computed every sample: +40 cycles a voice on the xd).
      const float p = positionPercent < 0.f ? 0.f : (positionPercent > 100.f ? 1.f : positionPercent * 0.01f);
      st[2] = 1u + (uint32_t)(p * (float)mask);
      const float t = sizePercent < 0.f ? 0.f : (sizePercent > 100.f ? 1.f : sizePercent * 0.01f);
      uint32_t len = 480u + (uint32_t)((float)(tableLen - 480u) * t * t * t);
      if (len > tableLen) len = tableLen;
      st[1] = len;
      const float f = fadePercent < 0.f ? 0.f : (fadePercent > 100.f ? 1.f : fadePercent * 0.01f);
      st[3] = 16u + (uint32_t)(f * (float)(len / 2u - 16u));
      st[4] = 1u;
      st[0] = 0u;
    }
    const uint32_t len = st[1];
    if (len == 0u) { *last = 0.f; return 0.f; }
    const uint32_t i = st[0];
    const uint32_t fl = st[3];
    const float toFloat = 1.f / 16383.f;
    if (st[4])
    {
      float att = 1.f;
      if (i < fl) att = (float)i / (float)fl;
      if (len - i <= fl) { const float a = (float)(len - i) / (float)fl; if (a < att) att = a; }
      float x = (float)buf[(w - st[2]) & mask] * toFloat * att;
      if (x > 2.f) x = 2.f; else if (x < -2.f) x = -2.f;
      table[i] = (int16_t)(x * 16383.f + (x < 0.f ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
    }
    float out = (float)table[i] * toFloat;
    if (st[4] && i < fl) out += *hold * (1.f - (float)i / (float)fl);
    *last = out;
    if (++st[0] >= len) { st[0] = 0u; st[4] = 0u; }
    return out;
  }

  // Stores one sample into a ring of int16 (over +-2). freeze (0 or 1) glides the stored value
  // from the input to what the slot already holds (~5 ms), so the buffer keeps looping its
  // content; once fully frozen the slot is left alone, so the loop doesn't wear down by
  // re-quantizing on every pass. The index keeps moving either way. A leaf.
  static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) void buffer_write(int16_t *buf, uint32_t mask, uint32_t *w, float in, float freeze, float *level)
  {
    *level += (freeze - *level) * 0.004f;
    const uint32_t i = *w & mask;
    *w = *w + 1u;
    if (*level > 0.9999f) return;
    const float old = (float)buf[i] * (1.f / 16383.f);
    float x = in + (old - in) * *level;
    if (x > 2.f) x = 2.f; else if (x < -2.f) x = -2.f;
    buf[i] = (int16_t)(x * 16383.f + (x < 0.f ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
  }
};

    {
      float y_n = 0.f;
      out[2 * i] = clip1m1f(y_n);
      out[2 * i + 1] = clip1m1f(y_n);
    }
  }

private:
  // The note a primitive that follows the played note (an oscillator's pitch, a TRACK filter)
  // reads: an effect gets none, so it's a fixed middle C.
  float note_;
  float noteFine_;
  // The fixed knobs' positions (0..1), as the device reports them.
  float time01_;
  float depth01_;
  float mix01_;
  // The device tempo in BPM, 120 until the device gives one.
  float tempo_;
  float *sdram_n;
  uint32_t grainSt_n[5];
  float prevTrig_n;
  float hold_n;
  float last_n;
  float positionPercent_n;
  float sizePercent_n;
  float fadePercent_n;
  uint32_t grainLen_n;

  // One sample of a looping grain (util/grain). st: [0] index, [1] length (0 = nothing yet),
  // [2] delay, [3] fade, [4] capturing. On a rising trig -- or, with selfTrig, at the start of
  // every pass -- it latches the delay (position 0..1 of the buffer, 1 = oldest), the length (size,
  // in samples) and the fade (0..1 of half the grain), then for length samples copies the buffer
  // at that constant delay into its own table (int16 over +-2, like the buffer), a fade-in and
  // fade-out of fade samples baked in, and afterwards loops the table until the next trigger.
  // What was playing at the trigger (*last) ramps out over the fade, so a retrigger doesn't
  // click. Inlined (always_inline): a call with its fourteen arguments cost more than much of
  // the body in grain-mill (xd emulator, 2026-10-01); code grows by a copy per voice.
  static inline __attribute__((always_inline)) float grain_step(const int16_t *buf, uint32_t mask, uint32_t w, int16_t *table, uint32_t tableLen, uint32_t *st, float *prevTrig, float *hold, float *last, float trig, int selfTrig, float positionPercent, float sizePercent, float fadePercent)
  {
    const float gate = trig >= 0.5f ? 1.f : 0.f;
    int start = gate > *prevTrig;
    *prevTrig = gate;
    if (selfTrig && !st[4] && st[0] == 0u) start = 1;
    if (start)
    {
      *hold = *last;
      // Position and size are only ever read here, so the clamps and SIZE's cube cost nothing
      // between triggers (they used to be computed every sample: +40 cycles a voice on the xd).
      const float p = positionPercent < 0.f ? 0.f : (positionPercent > 100.f ? 1.f : positionPercent * 0.01f);
      st[2] = 1u + (uint32_t)(p * (float)mask);
      const float t = sizePercent < 0.f ? 0.f : (sizePercent > 100.f ? 1.f : sizePercent * 0.01f);
      uint32_t len = 480u + (uint32_t)((float)(tableLen - 480u) * t * t * t);
      if (len > tableLen) len = tableLen;
      st[1] = len;
      const float f = fadePercent < 0.f ? 0.f : (fadePercent > 100.f ? 1.f : fadePercent * 0.01f);
      st[3] = 16u + (uint32_t)(f * (float)(len / 2u - 16u));
      st[4] = 1u;
      st[0] = 0u;
    }
    const uint32_t len = st[1];
    if (len == 0u) { *last = 0.f; return 0.f; }
    const uint32_t i = st[0];
    const uint32_t fl = st[3];
    const float toFloat = 1.f / 16383.f;
    if (st[4])
    {
      float att = 1.f;
      if (i < fl) att = (float)i / (float)fl;
      if (len - i <= fl) { const float a = (float)(len - i) / (float)fl; if (a < att) att = a; }
      float x = (float)buf[(w - st[2]) & mask] * toFloat * att;
      if (x > 2.f) x = 2.f; else if (x < -2.f) x = -2.f;
      table[i] = (int16_t)(x * 16383.f + (x < 0.f ? -0.5f : 0.5f));
    }
    float out = (float)table[i] * toFloat;
    if (st[4] && i < fl) out += *hold * (1.f - (float)i / (float)fl);
    *last = out;
    if (++st[0] >= len) { st[0] = 0u; st[4] = 0u; }
    return out;
  }
};

// unit.cc
// Generated by logue-patcher's logue-codegen.
// NOT hand-written -- do not edit directly, re-export instead.
#include "fx.h"
#include "unit_delfx.h"
#include "utils/int_math.h"

static Fx s_fx_instance;
static int32_t cached_values[UNIT_MAX_PARAM_COUNT];

__unit_callback int8_t unit_init(const unit_runtime_desc_t *desc)
{
  if (!desc)
    return k_unit_err_undef;
  if (desc->target != unit_header.target)
    return k_unit_err_target;
  if (!UNIT_API_IS_COMPAT(desc->api))
    return k_unit_err_api_version;
  if (desc->samplerate != s_fx_instance.getSampleRate())
    return k_unit_err_samplerate;
  if (desc->input_channels != 2 || desc->output_channels != 2)
    return k_unit_err_geometry;

  float *sdram = nullptr;
  const uint32_t sdramFloats = s_fx_instance.getBufferSize();
  if (sdramFloats > 0)
  {
    if (!desc->hooks.sdram_alloc)
      return k_unit_err_memory;
    sdram = reinterpret_cast<float *>(desc->hooks.sdram_alloc(sdramFloats * sizeof(float)));
    if (!sdram)
      return k_unit_err_memory;
  }
  s_fx_instance.init(sdram);
  for (int id = 0; id < UNIT_MAX_PARAM_COUNT; ++id)
  {
    cached_values[id] = static_cast<int32_t>(unit_header.params[id].init);
  }
  return k_unit_err_none;
}

__unit_callback void unit_teardown() { s_fx_instance.teardown(); }
__unit_callback void unit_reset() { s_fx_instance.reset(); }
__unit_callback void unit_resume() { s_fx_instance.resume(); }
__unit_callback void unit_suspend() { s_fx_instance.suspend(); }

__unit_callback void unit_render(const float *in, float *out, uint32_t frames)
{
  s_fx_instance.process(in, out, frames);
}

__unit_callback void unit_set_param_value(uint8_t id, int32_t value)
{
  value = clipminmaxi32(unit_header.params[id].min, value, unit_header.params[id].max);
  cached_values[id] = value;
  s_fx_instance.setParameter(id, value);
}
__unit_callback int32_t unit_get_param_value(uint8_t id) { return cached_values[id]; }
__unit_callback const char *unit_get_param_str_value(uint8_t, int32_t) { return nullptr; }

// UQ16.16 BPM (Korg's README; its templates convert it the same way).
__unit_callback void unit_set_tempo(uint32_t tempo)
{
  s_fx_instance.setTempo((tempo >> 16) + (tempo & 0xFFFF) / static_cast<float>(0x10000));
}
__unit_callback void unit_tempo_4ppqn_tick(uint32_t) {}
